display_name: Dispatch a work turn into a managed session
description: Fleet session-management, D2-window rider (rotation-boundary ruling 2026-08-04). Sends an arbitrary work turn (the 'text' argument) over the resolved host driver's driver channel (stream-json stdin) to the running Claude Code process behind agent_instance_id -- fire-and-forget, this call confirms the send, not the resulting turn. The bootstrap dispatch verb: spawn_session boots a worker with no first turn, so drive_session is how the steward hands a spawned worker its brief and every later follow-up turn. Driving a parked row un-parks it (the ledger's parked -> live edge, which this verb alone writes); every dispatch also re-arms the report-or-die deadline so freshly-assigned work is never instantly overdue. Only available on hosts whose driver provides a driver channel (currently 'headless' and 'tmux'); the degenerate 'operator' driver, and a headless/tmux process this build's memory no longer tracks (e.g. after a restart), both refuse with unsupported_on_host rather than silently doing nothing.
embedding_description: Send a work instruction, task brief, or follow-up prompt into a spawned fleet worker session over its live driver channel, un-parking it and refreshing its report-or-die deadline. Distinct from clear_session and compact_session (context hygiene, not work), from spawn_session (creates the worker process but sends it nothing), and from peer_send (peer messaging, not the worker's stdin channel).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: lifecycle_state (the row's state after this call) and unparked (true only when the row was parked and this dispatch drove the parked -> live transition).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call is fire-and-forget: a clean result confirms the text was written to the driver channel, not that the target session has read it, acted on it, or finished the turn. Follow-through is the worker's report_alive and the report-or-die sweep.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validates the text is non-empty, reads the managed_session ledger row, refuses on a terminal lifecycle_state, resolves the row's host driver, sends the text over its driver_channel(), re-arms report_by, then (parked rows only) writes the predicated parked -> live transition -- a fixed sequence, no retry loop.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: empty_text: nothing to dispatch -- the call was refused before any read. session_not_found: no managed_session row exists for the given agent_instance_id. lifecycle_state_conflict: the row is already terminated/retired -- terminal rows never receive driver-channel commands. unsupported_on_host: the row's host has no driver in this build, or its driver has no live driver channel for this host_ref (the degenerate 'operator' driver, or a headless process spawned before a restart wiped this build's in-memory tracking). illegal_lifecycle_transition / stale_lifecycle_state: the un-park write lost a race with a concurrent sweep or verb -- the text WAS already sent; re-read session_status before retrying.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For unsupported_on_host, deliver the work another way for that session (e.g. peer_send to an operator-attended session) -- this verb has no fallback path, by design, to avoid a silent no-op. For stale_lifecycle_state, the dispatch itself already reached the worker; only the un-park bookkeeping lost the race -- check session_status before re-driving, or the worker receives the same brief twice.
